scope: Assembled generic manager/index, cache and ownership; focus on publication, retirement cursor, insertion and typed cleanup.

findings.title: insert_at suppresses native head rereads
findings.observed: The port reads head once and reuses it for three first-node header writes and the final root-color operation. Source5DA61C reads tree,5DA625 and5DA629 reread it before min/max publication;5DA76A rereads it before loading root. The non-root branch also rereads tree after parent-link publication at5DA638/5DA645.
findings.reproduction_to_cover: Record native Memory reads of tree during the first manager index insertion, including header parent/min/max writes and final root color, and compare a Rust backend trace. Current tests record allocation/write/free and cannot detect these missing reads.
findings.minimum_correction: Reload tree head at the original source positions instead of carrying one cached head through the insertion. Retain existing Record allocation ownership.
findings.verification: Static instruction/source comparison; no compiler or new oracle executed in this review.

findings.title: insert_hint changes count/head/key read order
findings.observed: The port reads tree/head before tree.count and then reads node.key before checking head.min. Source5D2984 reads count first; the empty branch reads tree at5D2991. The nonempty branch reads tree at5D29B1 and head.min at5D29B9 before reading the node key on the minimum-hint branch at5D29BD.
findings.reproduction_to_cover: Trace the first empty insertion and the second minimum-hint insertion from the fixed manager hashes; assert count-before-head and minimum-before-key ordering. Add a read failure at each affected point to make the different first failing access observable.
findings.minimum_correction: Branch on count before loading head and delay node.key reads until the actual branch needs them, following5D2950.
findings.verification: Static instruction/source comparison; no compiler or new oracle executed in this review.

ownership_observations: Every successful manager allocation is inventoried before its fallible initialization; constructor failures use raw inventory retirement while the constructed flag remains false.
publication_attempted is set before the fallible global write, including the null allocation path; a failed publication remains represented until its explicit clear succeeds.
The retirement cursor advances only after a completed write or atomic release; the final global-clear failure keeps the completed action cursor and cannot trigger another free on retry.
Retirement planning is bounded to four tracked index nodes and nine distinct tracked sentinels and makes no writes before validation succeeds.

Temporary pending/Detached states preserve fresh buffers across copy publication errors; reset state advances after each successful564900 write and Group retains all failed slots in reverse cleanup order.
Cache hits borrow the provider value; MissFactory does not create a provider. Full lookup comparison ordering is directly asserted by the prepared cache trace tests.
nontermination_limits: Cache lower_bound and index search/iterator traversals have visited-node guards.

Index balancing assumes the private builder-owned tree stays structurally valid; this review did not prove termination under arbitrary allocator callbacks that rewrite tree topology. No such mutation exists in the inspected Windows allocation adapter.
verification_limits: No Rust execution in this review; root pipeline is responsible for qualification.
Native fixture success alone does not prove that unrecorded read order matches the Rust port.
No complete provider cache, real miss factory, populated manager destruction or nonempty UI claim.
